title_en: Machine learning from a business question
how_to_read: sentences[].w = first..last word id inside this chapter; word k (0-based) of the sentence is first+k and `ar` is the spoken text (its space-separated tokens are those words); fr = [start_frame, end_frame] at 24 fps from the word map; impact = hook words (id=text); num = spoken numbers with data-contract fact ids; first_mention = glossary terms to chip (id=term); dup = same claim in another chapter. Anchor with {word, lead_frames} only. Visual candidates are ideas, never footage.

constraints.anchors: {word, lead_frames} only; never seconds or frames; event frame = word start - lead_frames
constraints.lead_frames: kinetic word -3, graphic state change -2, shot cut -4..-6 (inside a pause >= 200 ms), counter starts at the number word
constraints.density: >= 20 events/min; no gap > 4 s without an event (hold <= 6 s with reason); shot median 6-12 s, max 25 s (shots > 12 s: an event every 3 s)
constraints.coverage: every sentence >= 1 anchored event; >= 80 % of sentences a mechanism event; every spoken number and every first-mention term on screen
constraints.kinetic: 8-20 kinetic words per minute; <= 6 words and <= 2 lines on screen; impact word 1-2 words
constraints.fx: hero (real-time 3D) <= 5 % of chapter frames (ADR-002 RT5); fx_tier lite|standard|hero
constraints.text: text on busy backgrounds needs a plate or halo; sizes and safe areas: 04 sections 3.2 and 3.4
banned: invented numbers (every number: data-contract id or source sentence)
constraints.components: use only frozen components (harness/schemas/components/); requests go to corpus/specs/_component_requests.jsonl
constraints.chapter_rhythm: problem -> mental model -> progressive visual -> worked example -> prediction -> failure (crit) -> fix (ok) -> callback -> artifact (per chapter, not per sentence)

sentences.ar: الـmachine learning بيبدأ بسؤال بيزنس وbaseline، مش بـalgorithm.
sentences.en: Machine learning starts with a business question and a baseline, not with an algorithm.

sentences.ar: لو قاعدة بسيطة أو SQL query بتجاوب السؤال كويس، النموذج مش تلقائياً أحسن هو بس أصعب في الشرح وأغلى في التشغيل.
sentences.en: If a simple rule or a SQL query answers the question well enough, a model is not automatically better — it is just harder to explain and more expensive to operate.

sentences.ar: فاكتب الـbaseline وقيسه. خمسة وستين ونص، متوسط خطأ مطلق.
sentences.en: So write the baseline down and score it. Sixty-five and a half, mean absolute error.
Now thirty houses we have sold.

sentences.ar: قاعدة السمسار بترسم خط بيغلط في الطرفين.
sentences.en: An estate agent's rule of thumb draws a line that misses at both ends.

sentences.ar: والخط المضبوط بيتحرك في مكانه من خلال الأدلة، وبيقلّل المسافة للنقط، وبيسجّل سبعة وتلاتة وتلاتين على داتا عمره ما شافها.
sentences.en: A fitted line pivots into place through the evidence, minimising the distance to the points, and it scores seven point three three — on data it has never seen.

sentences.ar: الجملة الأخيرة دي هي المنهج كله.
sentences.en: That last clause is the whole discipline.

sentences.ar: إنت ما بتحكمش على نموذج بالأمثلة اللي اتعلم منها؛ بتحكم عليه بداتا محجوزة، لأن النموذج اللي بيحفظ بيسجّل كامل وهو ما بيعرفش حاجة.
sentences.en: You do not judge a model on the examples it learned from; you judge it on held-out data, because a model that memorises scores perfectly and knows nothing.

sentences.ar: وده بيودّينا للـleakage، الـfailure اللي بينتج أكتر نتايج غلط مبهرة في المجال ده.
sentences.en: Which brings us to leakage, the failure that produces the most impressive wrong results in this field.

sentences.ar: تلات أنواع. عمود ما كانش موجود أصلاً وقت التنبؤ.
sentences.en: Three kinds. A column that would not exist yet at prediction time.

sentences.ar: وfeature مشتقة في الهدوء من الإجابة نفسها.
sentences.en: And a feature quietly derived from the answer.

sentences.ar: وصفوف من نفس المجموعة موجودة في التدريب والاختبار، فالنموذج بيتعرّف على المجموعة بدل ما يتعلم النمط.
sentences.en: And rows from the same group appearing in both training and test, so the model recognises the group rather than learning the pattern.

sentences.ar: وكل واحدة فيهم بتنتج score شكله انتصار وبينهار في production.
sentences.en: Each one produces a score that looks like a triumph and collapses in production.
Split by group, and the honest number appears.

sentences.ar: وانضباط الناس بتعدّيه: اضبط على الـvalidation، وافتح الـtest set مرة واحدة.
sentences.en: And one discipline that people skip: tune on validation, and open the test set once.

sentences.ar: كل بصّة زيادة على الـtest set هي مقدار صغير من التوفيق عليها إنت مش شايفه ومش قادر ترجّعه.
sentences.en: Every extra look at the test set is a small amount of fitting to it that you cannot see and cannot undo.

facts.rule: A number goes on screen with its fact id as `ref`/`data_refs`. `unmatched_numbers` are spoken but have no data-contract fact: their source is the sentence itself (a valid `s:` ref); never replace them with a different figure.

referenced.ctx: The fitted line beats the baseline 7.33 vs 65.50 MAE on held-out data.

glossary.rule: Explain the term in Egyptian Arabic the first time it appears; then use the original term naturally, in Latin script, inside Arabic sentences.
glossary.register_ar: Natural Egyptian, clear, calm, professional. Use إحنا and خلّينا نشوف and ببساطة where they help. No heavy Modern Standard Arabic. No exaggerated slang. Numbers are spoken naturally in Egyptian but displayed as Western digits.
glossary.register_en: Plain, direct, unhurried. Short sentences. No hype, no "imagine that…", no rhetorical questions that are not real prediction prompts. Say the number, then pause for half a beat before the next sentence — the pause is where the viewer reads the screen.
glossary.never_translate_rule: Explain them in Egyptian Arabic the first time they appear, then use the original term naturally.

first_mention_gloss.gloss_ar: إن معلومة من المستقبل دخلت التدريب

glossary.on_screen: Western digits, Latin terms in LTR isolates, Egyptian Arabic copy (no MSA), no per-letter animation (04 section 3.4).

concepts.failure: Evaluating a model on the same data it trained on, hiding overfitting and leakage.

concepts.def_en: The simplest reasonable reference result, such as a naive rule, average or timing before…
concepts.failure: Reporting a model's score without a baseline, so a trivial rule might score the same.

concepts.def_en: Structured Query Language: the standard declarative language for querying and changing da…
concepts.failure: Thinking SQL runs in written order; the engine plans execution in its own order.

concepts.def_en: A request to a database or search system to fetch, filter or change data; in SQL, usually…
concepts.failure: Blaming hardware for a slow query when a full table scan is the cause.

concepts.def_en: Information from the answer or the future sneaking into training, so test scores look excellent but fail on truly unseen data.
concepts.def_ar: الـleakage إن معلومة من الإجابة أو من المستقبل تدخل التدريب، فالنتايج تطلع ممتازة وتفشل على داتا جديدة فعلاً.
concepts.failure: Fitting scalers or encoders on all data before splitting, leaking test information into training.

concepts.def_en: An input column the model uses to predict; the label is the answer it must predict.
concepts.failure: Including a feature derived from the answer, which inflates scores through leakage.

concepts.def_en: The live environment where real users and real data are served, so changes there carry re…
concepts.failure: Testing or editing directly in production, risking accidental data changes and outages.

concepts.def_en: An automated check that runs code and asserts the expected result, so changes that break…
concepts.failure: Tests that never fail prove nothing; first watch the test fail, then fix.

concepts.def_en: An unordered Python collection that guarantees each element appears once and checks membe…
concepts.failure: Expecting a set to keep insertion order or allow indexing like a list.

metaphors.metaphor: Question → target → baseline bar the model must beat; train/test split = cutting a deck

components.does: One whole word (or a tatweel-joined compound like الـKafka) on screen; never split per letter.
Up to 6 kinetic words on at most 2 lines, each word arriving on its own spoken word anchor.
A technical term chip (Latin in an LTR isolate) with an optional Arabic gloss; 28 px floor if spoken.
A counter that rolls from the previous value to the target over the spoken number (preset count).
An arrow from a label to a target layer (or a named part of it, 'layer.part').
Failure beat: glitch + low thud; flashes stay <= 3/s (WCAG 2.3.1).
Fix beat: the target settles into place with a settle chime.
The shot camera: move + ease + intensity; drift always on; optional impact nudges (<= 4 px) on anchors.
Match cut between a layer of this shot and one of the next.
Lower-third caption for a source, term, speaker or location.
Draw an SVG path (stroke reveal; RTL by default for Arabic layouts).
Bars (single or stacked) with token colours; values carry refs.
A deck dealt into train/validation/test splits (seeded).
Trunk chapter title card (riser + sting in the SFX map).
